newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Telspec sees profit in next H1.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Telspec sees profit in next H1.

text.p: Telspec, the loss-making British telecommunications electronic equipment supplier, said on Thursday it was on its way to returning to profit in the next half year.
New chief executive Jonathan Paget told Reuters that after an "appallingly bad year", the company's trading performance had improved significantly in the last two quarters.

"We have a fourth quarter and now, to date, a first quarter, which give us confidence that in the first half as a whole, we will see a return to profitability," he said. But he added that a return to some of the explosive growth seen in the past would have to wait.
"This will really be a year of consolidation, with modest sales growth. I think in 1998 we can look forward to getting back to double digit sales growth with a refreshed product range," Paget added.
Telspec, who supplies customers such as British Telecommunications Plc, Deutsche Telekom AG and Telefonica de Espana SA, shocked the market with two profit warnings last year.

The company, which plunged into the red with an annual pre-tax loss of 9.9 million stg compared to a pre-tax profit of 8.7 million in 1995, has seen its shares crumble from a 12 month high of 870p to a low of 130p.
But relief at an upbeat results statement helped stabilise the stock, which rose 27.5p to 225p on Thursday.

Telspec, which has more than trebled in size since its listing around three years ago, blames last year's problems on poor sales forecasts resulting in materials being ordered which subsequently had to be written off and contracts being tendered for at unprofitable prices.
But Paget, who noted that the problems had mainly beset its European rather than Australian operations, said the group was firmly on a new track.
"I don't think I'd be so blunt if I were not confident that the main controls had been put in place -- although, of course, we have a long way to go," he said.

Hefty gearing of 91 percent and bank agreements to reduce 10.4 million stg of borrowings to 5.5 million by the end of this year were tough but not crippling, Paget said, adding that this provided a "very useful discipline" on the company internally.
"I am confident that we can...return to profitability within the constraints that the banks have put on us," he said.
As the group cuts its manufacturing costs through savings in materials and purchases, it plans to reinvest part of the savings into sales, marketing and product development.

Most of the group's products are "pair-gain" products -- electronics on telephone networks which allow the national telecoms company to carry more than one telephone channel on a single pair of copper wires.
With almost one customer per country, competition is becoming fiercer, but Paget noted that there were "an awful lot of countries".
